thread:
alex: Heads-up: Support flagged a customer hitting p99 ~2.8s on text-generation endpoints since ~03:00 UTC. They say it correlates with a spike in cold prefix misses.
liam: Thanks — any request IDs or example keys from their reports?
support-esc: pasted logs, sample requests: request_ids [rQ3f, rQ3g], prefixes look like user:acct:12345/session:abcd-efgh-ijkl. Appears many unique session suffixes.
sara: quick check — ops metrics show KV cache miss rate jumped from 8% -> 72% at 03:02. p95 went from 150ms -> 700ms, p99 ~2.8s.
liam: can you dump kv cache cardinality by prefix hash? run: `curl -s http://kv-metrics:9090/api/cardinality?prefix=user:acct:*`
ops-bot: scheduled job ran: cardinality ~1.2M active prefixes, top-heavy entropy on session suffix.
devon: that smells like a normalization issue. recent proxy change preserved full Authorization and X-Session-ID headers in cache key? We had a PR that included headers in key composition.
alex: PR #4521? That introduced header-based suffixing but only intended to use tenant-id. If X-Session-ID leaked into key, we get explosion of keys -> warmup + eviction thrash.
sara: log sample from node-03: `WARN kv_cache miss key="user:acct:12345:hdr:X-Session-ID=zzzz-1111" backend_miss=true ttl=2s`
liam: reproduce locally: run loadgen with varied session ids, observe cache churn and eviction loop. repro steps I used: 1) set CLIENT_SESSION_HDRS to include X-Session-ID 2) run `./loadgen --pattern=session-burst --qps=200` 3) monitor /metrics for kv_miss_rate.
devon: suggested mitigations: 1) roll proxy hotfix to strip X-Session-ID from key composition 2) temporarily increase prefix TTL to 30s and enable admission filtering for keys with high suffix entropy 3) adjust eviction to prefer LRU->LFU hybrid.
alex: Can we ship the proxy hotfix as a canary to one region? We need to confirm no functional regressions for customers relying on header-scoped behavior.
support-esc: customer confirms they don't rely on session-id in cache semantics.
liam: I'm patching proxy now: small diff to normalize_headers used_for_key = ["tenant-id"] (removes X-Session-ID). Deploy plan: canary to us-west-2, watch p99 and kv_miss.
sara: Also enabling short warmup jitter: `prefix_warmup_backoff_ms = jitter(50,200)` to avoid synchronized warmups.
devon: Added a guard in runtime: if unique_suffix_entropy(prefix) > 12 then mark suffix as non-keyed for admission for 60s. This avoids thrash while warmup populates shared prefixes.
liam: Deploying proxy canary...
ops-bot: deploy proxy-canary to us-west-2 started by liam at 3791122380
liam: Canary looks green so far — kv_miss_rate dropped to 18% after 90s, p95 back to ~180ms, p99 trending down.
support-esc: Customer reporting latency improved on their end too. :thumbsup:
sara: Next: longer-term fix - add deterministic prefix normalization in the SDK so we never include high-cardinality headers by default. Ticket created: INF-2019.
alex: Also add metric `prefix_key_entropy` per tenant to alert before it hits 50% miss threshold.
devon: I pushed runtime patch to repo branch `hotfix/prefix-normalize-entropy` with tests. Small config knobs: `prefix_entropy_threshold` and `suffix_admission_ttl`.
liam: rolling the proxy hotfix to 3 more regions after 15m observation window.
ops-bot: deploy proxy-canary promoted -> us-east-1 at 3791122440
sara: Reminder for postmortem: include timeline, root cause (header in key composition), mitigations (canary, warmup jitter, suffix admission), and follow-ups (SDK default normalization + alerting).
alex: Thanks everyone — great cross-team response. I'll start the PMF/incident doc.
liam: will follow up with the exact repro artifact and loadgen script in the runbook.
support-esc: closing loop with customer — will update ticket after full roll. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Note: automated rollback threshold set to p99>1.5s for 5m.
liam: last note: keep an eye on eviction stats for next 24h, if we see secondary hotspots we'll need shard-affinity adjustments.
